maria: Heads-up — onboarding Orchid-7B (7B decoder) quant sweep. AWQ/INT8 looks fine on CPU/triton-local, but when we run the same config via vLLM->Triton backend on H100 I see a ~3.6% BLEU-ish regression and occasionally garbled tokens.

devin: can you paste the exact command and the triton/vllm versions? also last logs from trtllm?

maria: repro steps below:

1) model -> Orchid-7B (fp16 -> awq-int8)
2) vllm 0.8.1 + tritonserver 2.29 + CUDA 12.2
3) driver: tensorrt-llm plugin loaded via /opt/trtllm

run:
```
vllm-server --model-path ./orchid-awq --backend triton --triton-url unix:///var/run/triton.sock --batch-size 4 --max-seq-len 1024
```

log excerpt (trtllm):
```
[TRTLLM] plugin loaded: libtrtllm.so (symvers 1.3.0)
[Triton] Backend trtllm failed to initialize: plugin symbol version mismatch
[CUDA] warning: kernel launch retry, status=UnknownError
[vLLM] fallback to CPU decode for 1/128 batches
```

maria: also, when trtllm initializes it reports a different FP8/INT8 kernel path than when we locally run tensorrt build. suspecting ABI mismatch with driver or libnvinfer

ashok: hmm, symbol version mismatch usually means the trtllm plugin was built against a different TensorRT/onnxruntime ABI. what are the libnvinfer versions on the host and inside triton container?

maria: host libnvinfer.so.8.6.0, inside triton container libnvinfer.so.8.6.1. they're close but not identical. LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the triton container is set to /usr/local/tensorrt/lib:/opt/trtllm/lib

leo: also check cuda driver vs toolkit. I've seen CUDA driver minor mismatch cause weird fp8 kernels to silently degrade. run `nvidia-smi` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` inside the container.

maria: nvidia-smi shows 535.104, driver header reports 535.104, toolkit 12.2. But triton container has a symlink to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so (different soname). Could be pick-up of host lib from earlier apt install.

devin: quick sanity checks:
- try LD_PRELOAD=/opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so before starting triton (force plugin order)
- run triton with --strict-model-config=false to avoid aggressive plugin validation
- try a minimal decode (batch=1, seq=128) to see if regression persists

ashok: also try building trtllm plugin with the exact inside-container headers. If you can't rebuild, set TRITON_ESCAPE_PLUGIN_CHECK=1 (internal env var) to skip symbol verification (not recommended for prod, but can confirm if mismatch is the cause).

maria: tried batch=1/seq=128 — accuracy looks identical to local run. Regression only appears when batching (continuous batching in vLLM). interesting.

leo: that suggests a batching kernel path difference. Maybe AWQ's quant kernels have different register allocations for multi-batch. Are there any warnings about kernel fallback in the CUDA logs? grep for 'fallback' or 'launch' in dmesg or triton logs.

maria: found further log:
```
[CUDA] cuLaunchKernel returned invalid configuration
[TRTLLM] falling back to slow generic kernel (correctness OK, perf degrade)
[vLLM] decode order altered to per-request sync
```

maria: fallback kernel fixes correctness but changes decode timing and tokenization boundaries -> small differences accumulate into the BLEU-style delta.

devin: ok we can treat this two ways: (A) fix plugin/driver so the fast kernel works, or (B) force vLLM/triton to use single-sample decode (avoid the batching kernel path) until we have a proper plugin build. For (A) we need to reproduce locally with the exact triton image and containerized libs then rebuild trtllm against those headers.

ashok: i'll spin a debug triton image with host libs mounted and run the plugin under gdb to catch the illegal launch. will report back with stack.

maria: temporary workaround for customer: set VLLM_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false and set TRITON_MAX_BATCH=1 — that eliminates the regression for now. shared the workaround in the ticket.

ops-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-179 — "Orchid-7B AWQ batching kernel fallback on trtllm". Assigned to @ashok and @devin.

devin: i'll open a GH issue in trtllm repo describing symbol mismatch + batched kernel fallback. tagging inference-kernel team. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trtllm/issues/482

leo: FYI we should add an entry to the onboarding checklist: verify triton/container libnvinfer sonames match host and add a quick-batch smoke test (batch=8 seq=512) to detect batching-kernel regressions early.

maria: thanks all. will keep thread updated. reassigning to ashok for the kernel trace.

ashok: started gdb run, seeing launch config mismatch on 3rd CUDA grid. dumping PTX and kernel params now. ETA ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: :thumbsup:"
